metadata.evidence_scope: site-level framing of Critical Theory and Social Justice
metadata.modeling_rule: Only the page's introductory framing is treated as Jude 3 site-level published content. Third-party excerpts and links are excluded from institutional attribution.

positions.summary: Jude 3's Critical Theory page characterizes Critical Theory as rooted in Marxism and contemporary Social Justice as an application of Critical Theory directed toward revolutionary social change.

The page argues that contemporary progressive social-justice efforts pursue identity-based equality across sexual, gender, and racial categories through deconstruction of traditional norms and redistribution of power.
positions.boundary: This records Jude 3's framing of the movement, not an independent research conclusion about all social-justice advocacy.

positions.summary: The page claims that similar Critical Theory and Social Justice efforts are evident within the PCA and other conservative denominations.
positions.boundary: This is preserved as Jude 3's organizational claim; it does not independently establish the classification of any named PCA person, church, seminary, or ministry.

positions.summary: The page describes the Critical Theory project as destabilizing traditional institutions, including Christian institutions, in the name of liberation or human flourishing.
